reading_rule: Primary method context and explicit model omissions. These references do not validate the new array geometry, optical coefficients, control authority or numerical coverage. No outside source bytes are redistributed.

sources.title: Fast, Minimum Storage Ray-Triangle Intersection
sources.read_scope: Author publication listing and retrieved seven-page primary paper mirror; PDF text extraction is incomplete. Used as algorithm attribution, not a full scholarly reading or adopted numerical tolerance specification.
sources.supports: The ray-triangle barycentric intersection construction used in the implementation.
sources.limits: The new implementation's tolerances, chunking, broad-phase culling, coincident-face handling and multilayer optical traversal are separately specified and tested assumptions. The cited method does not prove coverage under finite sampling.

sources.title: An Update to the NASA Reference Solar Sail Thrust Model
sources.authors: Andrew F. Heaton and Alexandra B. Artusio-Glimpse
sources.read_scope: NASA NTRS abstract and metadata, retrieved via the archival URL. The canonical page returned HTTP 403 during this review; no full-paper reading is claimed.
sources.supports: Established solar-sail thrust models include specular and diffuse reflection, thermal emission and non-Lambertian scattering terms; coefficients depend on the tested sail construction.
sources.limits: The present model implements only direct absorption, specular reflection and straight transmission with caller-supplied grey energy fractions. No coefficients or material validation are adopted from this source.

new_model_assumptions: Actual deformed triangle vertices determine face area, two-sided normals, direct-ray transmission and forces on every call.
Each face receives one centroid illumination sample; force is distributed equally among its three nodes, preserving total force, torque and affine virtual work.
Distinct forward crossings multiply scalar transmission. Coincident faces within the same tile merge using their minimum transmission; different tiles remain separate layers.
Finite-source quadrature is an explicitly constructed uniform-radiance spherical-cap rule, not a measured solar limb-darkening model or cited high-order quadrature.
Pressure is the sum of directional normal intensities divided by light speed. Converting a stated irradiance on the plane normal to the source centre requires the quadrature mean-cosine correction.

External eclipse transmission is a caller-supplied per-face and per-direction multiplier; it is recomputed from actual centroids and does not include diffraction unless the callback explicitly does so.

Receiver geometric coverage, any attenuating intersection and grey transmitted energy are distinct outputs. UV protection requires coefficients for that spectral band, not a broadband geometric inference.
No secondary reflected rays, diffuse scattering, thermal recoil or unmeshed opaque hardware is included. Spatial/source/time refinement remains necessary at boundaries and seams.
